newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's first nuclear plant fully operational.
newsitem.headline: Romania's first nuclear plant fully operational.

text.p: Romania's first nuclear reactor, a project plagued by repeated delays, has become fully operational, the plant's press office said on Thursday.
"The first unit of the nuclear power plant at Cernavoda has reached its nominal power," it said in a statement.

The 700-MW reactor at the plant at Cernavoda, on the River Danube, began operating in April. The reactor, already connected to the national grid, has undergone tests since and is gradually being taken up to full capacity.
The project has been coordinated by state-run Renel RA with assistance from a consortium grouping Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd and Italy's Ansaldo SpA.

The first reactor is expected to add some 660 megawatts to Romania's electric grid, which has an installed generating capacity of 21,701 megawatts. The plant is using some 40 megawatts for its own needs.

Cernavoda was started almost 20 years ago under the former communist regime. Work was halted in 1990 when a survey revealed some of the equipment was in poor condition and the welding was faulty. It restarted in 1991.
It was officially inaugurated earlier this year.
The Romanian plant was built with Canadian-developed Candu technology by Ansaldo.

The Balkan country has spent $10 billion on the project so far. With only one of its five proposed 700 megawatt reactors complete, Cernavoda is seen as a potential boon to Romania which imports around $1 billion worth of energy a year.
Its first reactor is capable of supplying up to 10 percent of the average electricity now produced in the country's coal, oil and hydro-powered electricity plants.
